findings.description: attacker_redirect_uri.lstrip('https://') strips a leading CHARACTER SET, not a prefix: https://hacker.example/cb -> acker.example. Three of five OAuth bypass variants produce corrupted hostnames; the authorize query was also not percent-encoded at all.
findings.impact: OAuth redirect_uri bypass experiments tested the WRONG host (corruption) or split the query string — invalid test payloads treated as valid, negative-control semantics weakened.
findings.fix_design: urlsplit-based _attacker_origin/_attacker_path (host[:port], IPv6 brackets, userinfo dropped, non-http(s) rejected) + quote()-encoded query params, encoded exactly once.
findings.regression_test: tests/test_umdr41_p0_correctness.py::test_5_2_* (8 tests: h/t/p/s hostnames, http/https, ports, paths, IPv4/IPv6, invalid schemes, userinfo, round-trip, negative control)

findings.description: UnifiedLogger (custom, (module, message) arity) lacked stdlib-name methods; any caller reflexively using logger.warning/critical would AttributeError. No such caller exists today (verified: only .warn/.error/.log used).
findings.impact: Latent; contract now documented + delegates added with same arity; wrong-arity calls fail loudly (TypeError).

findings.description: GLOBAL_SCOPE_REGISTRY is an in-process dict: policies loaded via POST /api/v1/scope/load are invisible to Celery workers, other Uvicorn workers, and vanish on restart. The worker receives scope_entries TEXT passed per-task, but the registry-based policy channel is not shared. A thread lock coordinates nothing across processes.
findings.impact: In multi-worker deployment the /scope/check endpoint and the worker can disagree on the authoritative policy; restart silently drops loaded policies.
findings.root_cause: No durable authority; per-process memory treated as global.
findings.fix_status: FIXED (opt-in) — SqliteScopeStore (versioned, append-only, WAL, tombstone-clear, recomputed-fingerprint tamper detection, ScopeStoreUnavailable fail-closed) + registry store mode + API bootstrap via WEBPENT_SCOPE_STORE_PATH; failure to init when requested is FATAL (no silent downgrade). Legacy no-store behavior preserved byte-for-byte.
findings.regression_test: tests/test_umdr41_scope_registry.py (8 tests, REAL subprocesses for cross-process visibility/versioning)
findings.residual_risk: Opt-in: deployments that do not set WEBPENT_SCOPE_STORE_PATH keep single-process semantics. Directive's alternative (explicit single-process restriction) documented in SECURITY_REVIEW.

findings.evidence: Route matrix in UMDR41_SECURITY_REVIEW.md; preflight code lines cited.

findings.description: RC-6 pool_after was derived from updated_hypotheses (the promote/abandon/retag update list) instead of the post-reducer pool: an empty update batch reported EVERY open hypothesis as 'distinguished' (false information gain), and DEFER/rabbit-hole updates were counted as resolutions.
findings.impact: Discovery-economics metrics overstated information gain; planner feedback misled.
findings.fix_status: FIXED — pool_after = before-pool minus PROMOTED/ABANDONED terminal ids (reducer-equivalent); new metadata updated_in_batch/_count separates upserts from resolutions.; UM-DR-41 §10.2 follow-up: challenger persistence across cycles added (rank_in_batch/batch_id/challenger_status on every coverage entry, cycle_count/last_batch_id on the ledger); the pre-existing umdr40 test was updated to the corrected contract with the rationale inline
findings.regression_test: tests/test_umdr41_rc6_rc7.py (4 tests: the exact false-positive scenario, terminal-vs-deferred, RC-7 original-rank semantics, bounded slice)
